item.title: Live Updates: Lindsay Clancy trial resumes with ex-husbands 911 call
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is standing trial on charges that she murdered her three young children in Duxbury, Massachusetts in 2023. Follow along for live updates on the second day of witness testimony.

item.title: Japan quake toll rises, people still missing in damaged mall and factory
item.description: The powerful earthquake that rocked southern Japan has killed at least 18 people and more remain missing in a damaged shopping mall and a paper factory.

item.title: Trump warns Iran is set to "get a beating" as 5-month war expands
item.description: The war in the Middle East is expanding, with Trump threatening Iran with "a beating" and the U.S. and Saudi Arabia jointly strike Iranian proxies in Iraq.

item.title: Singer-songwriter Glen Hansard killed in motorcycle crash
item.description: Academy Award-winning Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard has died in a motorcycle crash.

item.title: Newsom's taxpayer-funded California diaper program could "lead to waste," state records warned
item.description: Records reveal repeated warnings that Baby2Baby's plan to send every baby home with 400 diapers in limited sizes could lead to waste. The other finalist offered more diapers, more sizes and a direct-to-consumer option.

item.title: Schools are testing pepper-spraying drones to stop shooters
item.description: Schools in three states will be equipped with drones this coming academic year that aim to find and deter active shooters within seconds.

item.title: Japanese earthquake rescue workers race against time to find survivors at devastated mall
item.description: Emergency search and rescue crews are combing through the mangled wreckage of buildings after a devastating earthquake rattled southern Japan, killing over a dozen people. CBS News' Anna Coren has the latest details.

item.title: New video shows North Carolina woman's apparent last moments before she went missing in Grenada
item.description: Newly released surveillance video appears to show missing North Carolinian Liz Waddell just before she vanished while on vacation in Grenada. CBS News' Cristian Benavides has more on the investigation.

item.title: A look at the aftermath in Japan following deadly earthquake
item.description: Rescuers are still searching for survivors after a powerful earthquake hit southwestern Japan on Tuesday, killing at least 18 people. Four people died inside a shopping center that collapsed from an explosion one hour after the quake struck. Anna Coren reports.

item.title: 2025 was deadliest year for antisemitic attacks in 30 years, study says
item.description: Last year, 20 people were killed in antisemitic attacks outside of Israel, making it the deadliest year for such incidents since 1994.

item.title: Comey claims DOJ ordered illegal surveillance, seeks dismissal of "86 47" case
item.description: Former FBI Director James Comey filed new motions late Tuesday in his effort to toss out federal charges accusing him of threatening President Trump's by posting a photo of seashells arranged to form the numbers "86 47."

item.title: Watch Live: Fauci invokes 5th in hearing, citing Rand Paul's "unhinged obsession"
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci is testifying to the Senate on the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic, setting up a showdown between the infectious disease expert and GOP Sen. Rand Paul.

item.title: Tech workers sound the alarm on the risks of rapid AI development
item.description: The artificial intelligence industry faces internal pressure as developers at top technology companies caution that accelerating AI development is risky, emphasizing that the industry must pace itself and develop oversight. CBS News' Jo Ling Kent reports.

item.title: The Federal Reserve meets Wednesday. Could it raise interest rates?
item.description: The central bank is widely expected to stand pat on Wednesday, but persistent inflation concerns are reshaping expectations for the rest of 2026.

item.title: Trump and Zelenskyy find common ground on Russia-Ukraine war during White House meeting
item.description: President Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said their meeting at the White House went well. The two discussed licenses for Patriot interceptor missiles and diplomacy with Russia. CBS News' Aidan Stretch has more.

item.title: U.S. and Saudi Arabia strike Iran-backed groups in Iraq, CENTCOM stops Iran's "surprise attack"
item.description: After days of relative calm, the Middle East saw renewed fighting overnight. U.S. Central Command says it thwarted a "surprise attack" by Iran and joined Saudi Arabia in carrying out strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq. CBS News' Aaron MacLean and Olivia Rinaldi report.

item.title: Watch: Sen. Rand Paul blasts Fauci, demands apology at hearing on COVID-19 origins
item.description: Republican Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky opened a key panel hearing on the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic by demanding an apology from Dr. Anthony Fauci, the former top infectious disease expert for the federal government. Paul and Fauci have sparred for years, publicly accusing each other of lying.

item.title: Huge wildfires in Europe force thousands to evacuate as flames grow
item.description: Thousands of people are fleeing dangerous wildfires in France and Spain. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: Newly released surveillance video appears to show missing American in Grenada
item.description: Newly released video appears to show missing North Carolina mom Elizabeth Waddell's last known movements in Grenada as she entered the water, but does not show her returning. Two people on Jet Skis told local media they saw a woman, possibly Waddell, far from shore later that day and asked if she needed help but the woman declined. Cristian Benavides reports.

item.title: Actor Jared Leto accused of criminal sexual conduct by 4 women
item.description: Four women say Hollywood star Jared Leto committed sexual crimes against them when they were teenagers, in interviews with the BBC.

item.title: What happens if your ex stops paying a joint debt?
item.description: Joint debt doesn't disappear when a relationship does, and in most cases, lenders don't care who's to blame.

item.title: Apple unveils program to allow consumers to lease devices
item.description: Apple announced on Tuesday a new program called "Apple Upgrade," which allows consumers the option to lease new devices. It applies to everything from watches to laptops. Kelly O'Grady explains.

item.title: AI workers at major companies call for slowdown of the technology's development
item.description: Nearly 1,200 AI workers signed a letter on Tuesday, asking the U.S. government to slow down the development of the technology. Jo Ling Kent has more.

item.title: Americans face higher back-to-school costs. Here's what's pricier.
item.description: U.S. households will spend roughly $4,000 per student on school supplies and lunches this year, a new analysis found.

item.title: U.S. bans humanoid robot imports, eyeing China and national security concerns
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission is banning imports of new foreign-made humanoid robots and power inverters, citing national security risks, in a move that targets China.

item.title: Grants halted at agency devoted to safety of U.S. healthcare
item.description: Congress appropriated $345 million for the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality for the 2026 fiscal year, but the agency has spent less than $15 million on grants.

item.title: U.S. and Saudi Arabia strike "Iran-aligned terrorists" in Iraq
item.description: The U.S. and Saudi militaries announced airstrikes late Tuesday on Iranian-backed groups in Iraq, after Iran and its proxies allegedly targeted American forces.

item.title: Japan quake kills at least 13; more trapped in collapsed mall, factory
item.description: A major earthquake in Japan's southwest killed at least 13 people and left several injured or missing after a shopping center and a paper mill were heavily damaged.

item.title: Trump policy clears way for civil commitment of homeless in some states
item.description: In the year since President Trump signed an executive order aimed at moving homeless people off the streets, states have expanded involuntary treatment for the homeless.

item.title: Friend describes last known movements of missing American in Grenada
item.description: American Elizabeth Waddell was last seen on July 22 while visiting the tiny Caribbean island of Grenada.
